concept.technique_name: All from 9 and the last from 10 (Nikhilam Navatashcaramam Dashatah) with sub-sutra Proportionately (Anurupyena)

examples.problem_statement: Multiply $43 \times 47$ using the Vedic Mathematics technique for numbers near base 50.

solution.description: The two numbers sit just below 50, so take 50 as the working base; it is convenient because 50 is also 100 halved.

solution.operation: Write the numbers with their deviations from the base: 43 is -7 (since 43 - 50 = -7), 47 is -3 (since 47 - 50 = -3).
solution.description: Measure each number against that base: 43 falls 7 short and 47 falls 3 short, so the deviations are minus 7 and minus 3.

solution.operation: Calculate the left side: using method (a) add the numbers and subtract the base: 43 + 47 - 50 = 40. Alternatively, cross-add: 43 - 3 = 40 or 47 - 7 = 40.
solution.description: Build the left-hand part by adding the two numbers and removing one base, 43 plus 47 minus 50 gives 40; cross-subtracting instead, 43 minus 3 or 47 minus 7, gives the same 40.

solution.operation: Calculate the right side: multiply the deviations: (-7) × (-3) = 21.
solution.description: Build the right-hand part by multiplying the two deviations; both are negative, so their product is a positive 21.
Because the base is 50 rather than 100, the left-hand part carries a weight of 50: forty fifties is 2000, and adding the right-hand 21 gives 2021.
State the finished product: 43 times 47 is 2021.
Begin a second pass over the same problem by fixing the base again at 50, seen here as 100 divided by 2.
Recompute each number's distance from that base, 43 being 7 below it and 47 being 3 below it.

solution.operation: Calculate left side using any method:
solution.description: Announce the left-hand part, which can be reached by any of the three equivalent routes listed in the next steps.
First route to the left part: add both numbers and subtract one base, giving 40.
Second route: cross-subtract the other number's deviation from 43, which again gives 40.
Third route: cross-subtract the first number's deviation from 47, once more giving 40.
Multiply the two deviations for the right-hand part, since minus 7 times minus 3 is 21.
Weight the left part by the base and add the right part: forty fifties is 2000, and 2000 plus 21 is 2021.

solution.operation: Alternative method: Since base is 100/2, divide left side by 2: $40/2 = 20$
solution.description: Finish instead by treating the base as 100 halved: halve the left part so that 40 becomes 20, which can then be read straight off in the hundreds column.

solution.operation: Combine with right side: $20$ and $21$ gives $2021$
solution.description: Place the halved left part beside the two-digit right part, 20 followed by 21, which reads as 2021.
Start a third pass by naming the base once more as 50, or equivalently 100 divided by 2.

solution.operation: Calculate the deficits from the base: $43 - 50 = -7$ and $47 - 50 = -3$.
solution.description: Record the deficits from that base: 43 is 7 below it and 47 is 3 below it.

solution.operation: Find the left side of the answer: $43 + 47 - 50 = 40$ (alternatively, $43 - 3 = 40$ or $47 - 7 = 40$).
solution.description: Work out the left-hand part as 43 plus 47 minus 50, which is 40, with the cross-subtractions 43 minus 3 and 47 minus 7 confirming the same value.

solution.operation: Find the right side of the answer: $(-7) \times (-3) = 21$.
solution.description: Work out the right-hand part by multiplying the two deficits, which gives 21.

solution.operation: Combine the left and right sides: $(40 \times 50) + 21 = 2000 + 21 = 2021$.
solution.description: Join the parts using the base as the multiplier: 40 times 50 is 2000, and 2000 plus 21 is 2021.

solution.operation: Alternatively, using the $100/2$ base method: calculate the left side as $40$, then divide by $2$ to get $20$, and append the right side $21$ to get $2021$.
solution.description: Or finish the halving way: halve the left part 40 to get 20, then write the right part 21 after it so the answer reads 2021.
Both numbers sit just above 50, so measure them against base 50: 53 carries an excess of 3 and 52 an excess of 2.
First route to the left-hand part: add the two numbers and take one base away, 53 plus 52 minus 50, which is 55.
Second route: cross-add 53 to the other number's excess of 2, giving 55 again.
Third route: cross-add 52 to the first number's excess of 3, which also gives 55.
The right-hand part is the product of the two excesses, 3 times 2, which is 6.
Weight the left part by the base and add the right part: 55 fifties is 55 hundreds halved, or 2750, and 2750 plus 6 gives 2756.
These numbers sit just above 200, so switch the base to 200 and record the excesses: 207 is 7 more and 206 is 6 more.

key_reminders: {'point': "Sometimes it's easier to multiply by 100 and divide by 2, than multiply by 50."}
{'point': 'Choose whichever works for you.'}
common_mistakes: Multiplying the left-hand part by 100 instead of 50: in 43 x 47 the left part 40 stands for forty fifties, that is 2000, not 4000.
Dropping the minus signs on the deviations of 43 and 47 and then subtracting 21 instead of adding it.
Halving the right-hand part as well when using the 100-halved shortcut; only the left part is halved, so 40 becomes 20 while 21 stays 21.

concept.technique_name: Vedic multiplication using a base (Nikhilam adaptation with base 50)

examples.problem_statement: Multiply $43 \times 47$ using the Vedic Mathematics method for numbers near base 50.

solution.operation: Set up numbers with deviations from base 50: $43 = 50 - 7$ (deviation $-7$), $47 = 50 - 3$ (deviation $-3$).
solution.description: Anchor both numbers to base 50 and write each as the base less a shortfall: 43 is 50 less 7 and 47 is 50 less 3.

solution.operation: Compute left side: add the numbers, subtract the base, then divide by 2: $(43 + 47 - 50) / 2 = 40 / 2 = 20$.
solution.description: Find the left-hand part by adding the numbers, removing one base, then halving because 50 is one half of 100: 43 plus 47 minus 50 is 40, and half of 40 is 20.

solution.operation: Compute right side: multiply the deviations: $(-7) \times (-3) = 21$.
solution.description: Find the right-hand part by multiplying the two shortfalls; two negatives give a positive 21.

solution.operation: Combine left and right: the result is $20$ (left) and $21$ (right) giving $2021$.
solution.description: Write the halved left part and the two-digit right part side by side, 20 then 21, so the product reads 2021.
Begin a second pass by fixing the working base at 50.
Restate each number's distance from that base, 43 lying 7 below it and 47 lying 3 below it.
Compute the left part again by adding both numbers, subtracting the base and halving the result, so 40 becomes 20.
Two shortcuts reach the same left part: cross-subtract first and then halve, using either 43 minus 3 or 47 minus 7, each giving 20.
Multiply the two deviations to obtain the right part, which is 21.
Set the left part 20 against the right part 21 to read the product 2021.

solution.operation: Identify the base as 50. Find the deviations from the base: 43 is -7 and 47 is -3.
solution.description: Start a third pass by naming base 50 and its two deviations, minus 7 for 43 and minus 3 for 47.

solution.operation: Calculate the left side using one of three methods: a) $(43 + 47 - 50) / 2 = 40 / 2 = 20$, b) $(43 - 3) / 2 = 40 / 2 = 20$, c) $(47 - 7) / 2 = 40 / 2 = 20$.
solution.description: Collect the three equivalent routes to the left part: adding the numbers and removing the base, or either cross-subtraction, all give 40, which halves to 20.

solution.operation: Calculate the right side by multiplying the deviations: $(-7) \times (-3) = 21$.
solution.description: Take the right part as the product of the deviations, which is 21.

solution.operation: Combine the left side (20) and the right side (21) by placing them side-by-side to get the final answer: 2021.
solution.description: Place 20 and 21 next to each other to finish the product as 2021.

common_mistakes: Forgetting to halve the left-hand part: writing 40 beside 21 gives 4021 instead of 2021.
Halving the right-hand part too; only the left part is halved, because the base 50 is half of 100.
repair_note: Wrote all 14 empty descriptions so each narrates its own operation across the three passes over 43 x 47. Technique name and arrow_matrix scaffold already matched the base-50 halving method and were kept. Added two common_mistakes about the halving step.

solution.description: Since both numbers are close to 10, we use 10 as the base for the Nikhilam method.
For each 7, we calculate how much it differs from the base 10. Since 7 is 3 less than 10, the deviation is -3.
Take the left part either by cross-adding 7 to the other seven's deviation of minus 3, or by adding both sevens and removing one base; 7 minus 3 and 7 plus 7 minus 10 both give 4.
Multiply the deviations together to get the right part of the answer. Negative times negative gives positive.
The left side (4) and right side (9) are combined to form the final answer.

common_mistakes: Writing the right-hand part as minus 9: both deviations are minus 3, and a negative times a negative gives plus 9.
Forgetting to remove the base on the left, so 7 plus 7 is left as 14 instead of being reduced to 4.

Corrected technique_name from the bare 'squaring' to name the base-deviation method the steps actually use, and the scaffold from place_value_chart to arrow_matrix, since the steps manipulate cross-subtracted deviations rather than place-value columns. concept.sub_category: Ekadhikena Purvena (One More than the Previous)

solution.operation: Identify the base (10) and the number of digits (2)
solution.description: Note that 65 has two digits and ends in 5, which is exactly the setting where Ekadhikena Purvena applies, with base 10 and a split after the leading digit.

solution.operation: Separate the number into two parts: the part before 5 (n) and the last digit (5)
solution.description: Split the number into the part standing before the 5, which is n equal to 6, and the final digit 5.
Multiply that leading part by the next whole number up, 6 times 7, which gives 42 for the front of the answer.

solution.operation: Append 25 to the result from step 3
solution.description: A number ending in 5 always squares to something ending in 25, so write 25 immediately after the 42.
Read the two blocks together as one number: 65 times 65 is 4225.
Set the leading digit 4 against its successor 5 on the left, and the two final fives against each other on the right, as one more than the previous requires.
Evaluate the two products separately: 4 times 5 is 20 and 5 times 5 is 25.
Set 20 in front of 25 to read the square, 2025.
Here the leading digit is 5, so pair it with its successor 6 on the left while the two final fives multiply on the right.
Evaluate the two halves: 5 times 6 is 30 and 5 times 5 is 25.
Put 30 in front of 25 to get 3025.
With 9 in front, the left product is 9 times its successor 10, and the right product is again 5 times 5.
Work them out: 9 times 10 is 90, while the right-hand block stays 25.
Join 90 and 25 to read the square, 9025.
For a three-digit number the leading part is everything before the 5, here 11, so the left product is 11 times 12 while the right is still 5 times 5.
Work them out: 11 times 12 is 132, and the right-hand block is 25.
Write 132 ahead of 25 to give 13225.

key_reminders: {'point': "The page identifies this method as a 'second corollary' of the sutra 'All from 9 and the last from 10'."}
{'point': "It works best for 125^2 and less.'"}

Splitting 115 as 1 and 15 rather than 11 and 5, which gives 1 times 2 instead of the correct 11 times 12.
Shortening the right-hand block to a single 5; for any number ending in 5 the last two digits are always 25.

solution.operation: Apply Nikhilam Sutra: (Base + cross sum of deviations) | (Product of deviations)
solution.description: The formula is (Base + (d1 + d2)) | (d1 × d2) where d1 and d2 are deviations

solution.operation: Calculate left part (Base + sum of deviations)
solution.description: Add the base to the sum of the deviations (-8 + -2 = -10)
Multiply the deviations, remembering that negative times negative is positive

Multiply deviations: 58 x 52 = 3016
Adjust for negative: -10 becomes 100-10=90
Right part: last 2 digits of 3016 is 16
Combine parts: 90 and 16 gives 2016
Verify: 42x48=2016
Final answer is 2016

examples.problem_statement: Multiply the numbers 151 and 159 using the Vedic Mathematics technique for numbers where the first parts are the same and the last parts add up to 10.

solution.operation: Identify that the first parts are the same ($4$) and the last digits add up to $10$ ($2 + 8 = 10$).
Multiply the first part by one more than itself: $4 \times (4+1) = 4 \times 5 = 20$.
Combine the results: the left part is $20$, the right part is $16$ (two digits), giving $2016$.
Identify that both numbers start with 15, and the last digits (1 and 9) add up to 10
Multiply the left part (15) by one more than itself: $15 \times 16 = 240$
Since we're working in base 100, write the right part with two digits: 09
Combine the results: $240$ and $09$ to get $24009$
Identify that both numbers start with the same left part ($4$), and the right digits add up to $10$ ($2 + 8 = 10$).
Multiply the left part by one more than itself: $4 \times 5 = 20$.
Multiply the right digits by each other: $2 \times 8 = 16$.
Combine the two results to get the final answer: $2016$.

solution.operation: Write digits: 6 and 3 under 63; 9 and 8 under 98
solution.description: Set 63 above 98 with the digits aligned so the vertical and crosswise pattern can be applied.
Multiply vertically at each end: the tens digits give 6 times 9, or 54, on the left, and the units digits give 3 times 8, or 24, on the right.

Add the second carry to the left block, 54 plus 7, which is 61.
Read the reduced blocks from left to right, 61 then 7 then 4, giving 6174.

Reduce the right block first: 32 leaves 2 in the units place and carries 3.
Add that carry to the middle block, 12 plus 3 is 15, so write 5 and carry 1.
Add the remaining carry to the left block, 1 plus 1, which is 2.
Read the reduced blocks in order, 2 then 5 then 2, giving 252.

concept.technique_name: Vertically and crosswise multiplication of a three-digit by a two-digit number (Urdhva Tiryagbhyam)

examples.problem_statement: 104 x 98 (using this rule for a sum we calculated with deficiencies from the base)

solution.description: Write 104 above 98 with the units aligned, which sets out the columns the vertical and crosswise pattern will work through.
Begin at the right-hand end by multiplying the units digits, 4 times 8, which is 32.
Move one column left and cross-multiply that pair, 0 times 8 plus 4 times 9, which is 36.
Move left again and cross the outer digits with the inner ones, 1 times 8 plus 0 times 9, which is 8.
Finish the pattern at the left-hand end by multiplying the leading digits, 1 times 9, which is 9.
List the four partial results in column order from left to right as 9, 8, 36 and 32, before any carrying is done.

solution.operation: Carry over from right: 32 → write 2, carry 3; 36+3=39 → write 9, carry 3; 8+3=11 → write 1, carry 1; 9+1=10 → write 10
solution.description: Reduce the columns from the right: 32 keeps 2 and carries 3; 36 plus 3 is 39, keeping 9 and carrying 3; 8 plus 3 is 11, keeping 1 and carrying 1; and 9 plus 1 is 10 at the front, so the product reads 10192.

key_reminders: {'point': 'Go right to left\nWork right to left carry over\nRemember: The overall pattern is VERTICAL/CROSS/CROSS/VERTICAL.'}
{'point': 'The middle parts are obtained by adding the crosswise multiplications.'}
{'point': 'Outer parts are vertical multiplication.'}
{'point': 'Speed tip: This method allows you to compute digit-by-digit without writing down partial products separately, reducing steps and mental load.'}
